content: Bovine coronavirus (BCV) is a member of the Coronaviridae family, which consists of enveloped, single-stranded, positive-sense RNA viruses characterized by their club-shaped surface projections. This virus is responsible for causing Calf Enteritis and contributes to the Enzootic Pneumonia Complex in calves. In adult cattle, it can lead to Winter Dysentery. BCV has the ability to infect both domestic and wild ruminants and is distributed worldwide. Transmission occurs horizontally, primarily through oro-fecal or respiratory routes. In calves, infection typically occurs between the ages of one week and three months. Gastrointestinal symptoms include severe diarrhea, dehydration, depression, reduced weight gain, and anorexia. Respiratory infections in calves manifest as a serous to purulent nasal discharge. Clinical signs may worsen if secondary bacterial infections occur. In adult cattle, infections are usually subclinical, except in cases of Winter Dysentery, which primarily affects housed cattle during the winter months. Winter Dysentery is characterized by profuse diarrhea and a significant reduction in milk yield. A presumptive diagnosis can be made based on the history and clinical signs. Definitive diagnosis of enteric coronavirus infection is achieved through electron microscopy or an ELISA test performed on fecal or tissue samples. For respiratory disease, diagnosis is confirmed by performing a direct fluorescent antibody test on nasal washes, which identifies the viral antigen. The haemagglutination inhibition test can be used to determine the specific strain of coronavirus. Treatment for BCV infection is primarily symptomatic. Disease control can be achieved by vaccinating pregnant dams with a live vaccine (ATCvet code QI02), which provides antibodies to the virus in the colostrum. Additional management strategies, such as ensuring adequate colostrum intake in newborn calves, maintaining proper hygiene, and improving ventilation in housing facilities, can help reduce the incidence of the disease.
